root_cause: Saved replay begins interception only after the loading event and accepts tab-only events. Initial requests can precede interception; delayed responses from the old document can satisfy the new run.
design: Service-worker-owned scoped CDP lease installs Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument and Runtime binding before Page.reload. No raw CDP Network capture.

Binding events are joined to Chrome Runtime executionContextId and system-unique uniqueId for the main default frame. Pre-reload contexts are rejected; a replacement document, including same-URL navigation, terminates the run.
A per-run early event queue bridges context creation and frame commit, budgeted from the existing maxBodyBytes option. Existing capture window bounds lifecycle; no new global cap or timing constant.
A private extension runtime Port avoids generic message payload logging. Port disconnect and cancellation release owned resources; the SW path uses the same owner directly.

Tap emits only whitelisted response data and hashed request identity; headers are omitted in binding mode. Cleanup preserves manual capture that reused the tap and CDP attachments retained by other clients.

alternatives.late_relay: Rejected: retains document-start race even with sender.documentId.
alternatives.raw_cdp_network: Rejected: exposes raw request headers/postData to the capture boundary.
alternatives.dynamic_content_scripts: Not selected: registration matches URLs across tabs and needs static script/config coordination; weaker per-tab ownership than the existing CDP primitive.

prepared_tests: Initial binding response before frame commit survives; delayed old context is rejected; registration precedes reload; sensitive header canaries omitted.
Cancellation during deferred script registration removes the late script before releasing lease and never reloads.
Same-URL replacement context cancels capture and cannot contribute rows.
blocking_integration_work: Existing cdp_attach is privileged and admin-only; data_patterns is action-tier. Scratch transport currently lacks authorization integration. Reuse the existing debugger approval/admin/Pilot checks before acquireSession; never deploy this adapter as written.
Core and adapters are not typechecked or executed. Review CDP attach/detach lease races, unsupported uniqueId behavior, frame/context ordering and cleanup failure propagation.
Complete actual runNetworkCapturePattern caller, private-port and shared-lease tests; existing core tests alone are not sufficient assurance.
acceptance: Guarded baseline red for early request and delayed old-document selection; fixed real-mode/caller green.
Mutation removing document identity must fail downstream row/provenance assertions, not merely helper checks.

Borrowed/concurrently retained debugger attachment survives cleanup; owned attachment and new-document registration are removed on success, timeout, cancellation, tab close, navigation and partial setup failure.
Denied debugger approval never attaches or reloads and reports a truthful error.
Installed real Chrome repeat-run captures initial load request; old document high-sequence response never wins; same-URL navigation cannot be misattributed.
Typecheck and required handler catalog generation after integration; no build during freeze.
risks: Top-frame fetch/XHR only; workers/subframes are not covered.
Cross-URL redirects are currently treated as navigation interruption; review intended redirect behavior.
Runtime uniqueContextId support and Chrome event ordering need actual-browser verification.
Per-run early byte budget may reject a burst; rejection must be explicit, never partial success.
Main-world binding cannot authenticate arbitrary hostile page content; trusted Chrome context identity proves document provenance only.
